video.transcriptSummary: This course is a living meta-build reference model: every single stage you study is backed by the real markdown specs, ADRs, hooks, skills, and code that built Antigravity Academy itself. Starting from Stage 1 (cf-research), you see how dependency auditing caught GSAP's proprietary EULA before a single package was installed. In Stages 2 and 3 (cf-grill-me + cf-plan), five crisp questions locked our isolated Next.js App Router architecture in ADR-0002 and froze Zod schemas in plans/antigravity-academy-spec.md. In Stage 4 (cf-implement), Task 0 froze shared interfaces so four parallel Swarm workers built the Backend APIs, Three.js 3D Engine, Glassmorphic UI, and Vitest suite without a single overlapping file edit. In Stages 5 and 6 (cf-qa-review + cf-deploy-staging), an independent cf-reviewer audited security boundaries while the browser subagent verified 375px, 768px, and 1440px viewports prior to a HITL-gated Vercel preview deploy. Finally, Stages 7 and 8 (cf-triage + cf-learn + cf-handover) show how to convert lessons into permanent rules and add Course N+1 in any future conversation.

steps.title: Stage 1 — Research: Discovery, Trade-Offs & License Auditing
steps.summary: In 'The New SDLC With Vibe Coding' and 'Human Judgment Doesn't Leave the Software Factory, It Relocates', generation is cheap while intent and risk discovery move upstream. Stage 1 (`cf-research`) inspects the workspace, audits licenses/CVEs, and maps trade-offs in `.memory/research*.md`.

eli5.plainTitle: Station 1: Look Before You Leap (Research & Safety Check)
eli5.oneLineHook: Before building a single piece, inspect what already exists and check that every borrowed tool is free and safe to use.
eli5.everydayAnalogy: Checking your pantry and reading food labels carefully before you start cooking dinner.
eli5.simpleExplanation: When AI can build pages in minutes, the biggest mistake is rushing straight into building the wrong thing—or grabbing a borrowed tool that has hidden legal strings or safety bugs. Station 1 pauses for ten calm minutes first. Your helper inspects what is already in your project folder, compares two or three sensible ways to solve your goal, checks every tool's permission label, and writes a clear summary note for you to approve.
eli5.whyItMatters: Catching a bad tool choice or folder conflict on Day 1 takes five minutes to swap. Discovering that same problem a week later after building twenty pages means painful rewrites and wasted time.
eli5.roleInProtocol: This is the front door of the 8-Station Code Factory. During the real build of this very Academy, Station 1 spotted a restricted animation library license before line one was written and swapped in a free, open alternative automatically.
eli5.howToUseGoingForward: Start every new project or major feature with a quick Research check that compares options and verifies permissions—and never let building begin until you read and approve that short summary.
eli5.whenToUse: Use this at the very beginning of any new project, before adding a new outside tool or plugin, or whenever you want to compare two or three ways to solve a problem safely.
eli5.realWorldExample: While planning this very Academy website, our Station 1 check noticed a popular animation helper had a paid commercial license restriction. It flagged the risk immediately and picked a clean open-source option instead—saving hours of rework before a single page existed.
eli5.audioScript: Welcome to Course Two, Station One: Look Before You Leap. Imagine deciding to cook a big meal without opening the fridge or reading the labels on the jars. You might grab expired milk or realize halfway through that you are missing a pan. Building software with AI is the exact same. Because AI can create files so quickly, smart builders pause at Station One first. Your helper inspects your existing folders, compares two or three clean options, checks that every outside tool is free and safe, and hands you a short summary note. Only after you give a calm thumbs-up does the factory move to Station Two.
eli5.diagramCaption: How Station 1 inspects your folder, checks tool permissions, and pauses for your thumbs-up before anyone writes code.

keyTakeaways: Human Judgment Moves Upstream: Because agents eliminate syntax translation friction, engineers focus first on problem intent, architecture constraints, and risk boundaries before a single line is generated.

Live Meta-Build Win: During Stage 1 of Antigravity Academy, dependency inspection flagged GSAP's proprietary Webflow Standard License and immediately replaced it with MIT-licensed `motion` before any code was written.

Plugin Root Isolation constraint discovered early: because the repo root is symlinked into `~/.gemini/config/plugins/code-factory`, the web platform had to live inside `academy/` to keep plugin discovery spotless.
Every research doc ends with a human Outer-Loop Sign-Off Gate confirming trade-offs, licenses, and security posture.
actionChecklist: Open `.memory/research-academy-platform.md` in the Repo Explorer to inspect the full dependency compliance table.
Verify every new package has a permissive license (MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD/ISC) and zero known High/Critical CVEs.
Require explicit human sign-off on architectural trade-offs before opening Stage 2.

steps.title: Stage 2 — Spec: Interrogating Ambiguity & Locking Contracts
steps.summary: Ambiguous requirements turn autonomous factories into Dark Factories shipping the wrong intent. Stage 2 pairs `cf-grill-me` (up to 5 sharp decision questions) with `cf-plan` to lock Zod contracts, Selective Autonomy tiers (Lights-Out vs. Human-Lit), and verification oracles in `plans/<feature>-spec.md`.

eli5.plainTitle: Station 2: Ask 5 Sharp Questions & Lock the Exact Blueprint
eli5.oneLineHook: Clear up fuzzy wishes upfront with five quick questions so your AI builds the exact app you pictured—not a wild guess.
eli5.everydayAnalogy: Agreeing on exact room sizes, paint colors, and budget with a house builder before anyone swings a hammer.
eli5.simpleExplanation: If you tell a builder 'make me a nice kitchen,' they might install purple cabinets when you wanted warm wood. Station 2 stops guesswork cold. First, your helper asks up to five sharp, friendly questions to uncover any fuzzy spots—like where information is saved, what happens when a button fails, and what we are leaving out for later. Then it writes one clear, locked blueprint listing exactly what finished looks like.
eli5.whyItMatters: Fuzzy instructions create 'surprise software' where an AI happily builds fast in the wrong direction. Five minutes of clear questions upfront prevents hours of frustrating back-and-forth edits later.
eli5.roleInProtocol: Station 2 turns rough wishes into a rock-solid written blueprint inside `plans/`. It also marks which parts AI can check automatically and which sensitive parts—like logins, payments, or publishing—always require a human pause.
eli5.howToUseGoingForward: Whenever you have a new feature idea, ask your AI to interview you with up to five short questions first, then review the written blueprint and Non-Goals list before giving the green light.
eli5.whenToUse: Use this right after Station 1 Research—or anytime your idea has open choices about appearance, saved data, user accounts, or how you will check that it works.
eli5.realWorldExample: Before building this Academy, five quick questions locked everything in two minutes: save beginner progress right in the browser for version one, use a sleek dark studio theme, keep safety checks pure and instant, and hold off on complex user logins until version two.
eli5.audioScript: Now we arrive at Station Two: asking sharp questions and locking the blueprint. Think of hiring someone to remodel your kitchen. If you only say make it nice, you might come home to neon green counters. So before a single tool comes out, Station Two runs a quick, friendly interview—at most five high-impact questions to clear up every gray area. Where should progress be saved? What should happen if a screen is empty or hits an error? What are we intentionally skipping for now? Once you answer, your helper locks one clear blueprint so every builder knows the exact finish line.
eli5.diagramCaption: How five quick questions remove guesswork and produce a clear, locked blueprint before building starts.

keyTakeaways: Lit vs. Dark Factory Spec Discipline: Every `cf-plan` spec classifies tasks into Lights-Out (crisp machine oracle) vs. Human-Lit (auth, security/RLS, finance, infra, core architecture) and declares the exact verification oracle upfront.

Live Meta-Build Win: `cf-grill-me` locked 5 decisive calls in under two minutes—Next.js App Router over raw HTML, stateless v1 `localStorage` + Zod, dark glassmorphic palette, unified `VideoStage`, and pure TypeScript HITL simulation.
Every API endpoint specifies its exact Zod schema, pagination defaults (`limit=20`, `max=100`), Vercel `maxDuration`, and 4xx/5xx error codes before implementation begins.
Explicit Non-Goals prevent scope creep during Swarm execution (e.g., deferring Supabase Auth + Postgres RLS cleanly to v2).
actionChecklist: Inspect `plans/antigravity-academy-spec.md` in the Repo Explorer to see how Zod contracts and UI state matrices are specified.
Never skip `cf-grill-me` when a request leaves persistence, auth, or visual direction ambiguous.
Verify the locked spec lists explicit Loading, Error, Empty, and WCAG 2.1 AA states for every interactive component.

steps.title: Stage 3 — Architecture: System Maps, ADRs & Design Tokens
steps.summary: Durable decisions belong in `.memory/decisions/` (ADRs) and `.memory/architecture.md`, not buried in ephemeral chat history. Stage 3 freezes boundaries, rejected alternatives, Tailwind v4 `@theme` design tokens, and non-overlapping file partitions.

eli5.plainTitle: Station 3: Draw the Floor Plan & Assign Separate Workbenches
eli5.oneLineHook: Write down why you chose your design and give every helper their own separate room so nobody bumps elbows.
eli5.everydayAnalogy: Drawing a house floor plan and assigning the painter, electrician, and carpenter to separate rooms.
eli5.simpleExplanation: Chat messages scroll away and get forgotten, so Station 3 saves your big design choices in permanent project notes—explaining what you picked, what you turned down, and why. It also creates one shared color and style sheet so every page matches, and divides the upcoming building work into separate, non-overlapping zones so multiple helpers can work at once without ever editing the same file.
eli5.whyItMatters: Without a written floor plan and separate zones, two helpers trying to build fast will accidentally overwrite each other's files, pick mismatched colors, or re-argue decisions you already settled yesterday.
eli5.roleInProtocol: Station 3 creates your durable Decision Notes (`.memory/decisions/`) and divides the project into Step 0 (shared connections) plus clean parallel workbenches so Station 4 can run smoothly at full speed.
eli5.howToUseGoingForward: Before letting multiple helpers work in parallel, make sure every big choice has a short 'Why We Picked This' note and each helper has a crystal-clear list of files they own—and files they must not touch.
eli5.whenToUse: Use this whenever a project has more than two or three moving parts, when you want consistent colors across many screens, or right before launching a parallel team of helpers.
eli5.realWorldExample: For this Academy, Station 3 saved Decision Note 0002 explaining why we kept all colors in one central style sheet and split building into four separate zones: Data & Courses, 3D Visuals, Page Layout, and Automatic Tests—zero file collisions!
eli5.audioScript: Welcome to Station Three: drawing the floor plan and assigning separate workbenches. Imagine building a house where the painter, plumber, and carpenter all crowd into the exact same tiny closet at once—chaos! And imagine forgetting next month why you placed a wall in a certain spot. Station Three solves both problems. First, it writes down your big design choices and why you made them in permanent project notes instead of letting them vanish in old chat history. Second, it sets up one shared style palette and splits the upcoming build into clean, separate workbenches so helpers can work side by side without ever bumping elbows.
eli5.diagramCaption: How Step 0 locks shared rules and colors first so four separate workbenches can build side by side with zero overlap.

keyTakeaways: Live Meta-Build Win: `ADR-0002` explicitly documents why direct imperative Three.js islands beat `@react-three/fiber` (zero React 19 peer friction + full WebGL/DPR/IntersectionObserver control) and why build-time allowlisted repo sync prevents secret leaks.
Design System Invariant: All colors, typography (`Space Grotesk` + `JetBrains Mono`), and glass surfaces live in `globals.css` `@theme` tokens—zero hardcoded hex values in UI components.
Partition Planning: Decomposing the work into Task 0 (shared schemas/tokens) + Tasks 1–4 guarantees parallel agents never overwrite each other's files.
actionChecklist: Read `.memory/decisions/0002-academy-nextjs-glassmorphic-architecture.md` in the Repo Explorer.
Check that every ADR records Context, Decision, Alternatives Considered, and Consequences.
Confirm Task 0 freezes all shared TypeScript interfaces (`schemas.ts`, `contracts.ts`) before launching parallel builders.

steps.title: Stage 4 — Build: Task 0 Lock & Non-Overlapping Swarm Execution
steps.summary: Execution (`cf-implement`) strictly follows the locked spec. The orchestrator completes Task 0 first, then fans out clean `cf-backend` and `cf-frontend` workers onto strictly non-overlapping file partitions—preventing context rot and merge conflicts.

eli5.plainTitle: Station 4: Build Side by Side Without Stepping on Toes
eli5.oneLineHook: Finish the shared connecting pieces first, then let focused helpers build their own pieces calmly at the exact same time.
eli5.everydayAnalogy: Four friends building the four corners of a giant jigsaw puzzle at once after locking the border pieces first.
eli5.simpleExplanation: Now the actual building happens—and because Stations 1 through 3 did the careful thinking, Station 4 feels calm instead of frantic. First, one lead helper finishes the shared connecting pieces (Step 0) so every puzzle edge matches. Next, specialist helpers fan out onto their own separate folders and build strictly what the blueprint asked for—no unapproved surprises, no messy file clashes, and quick checkups along the way.
eli5.whyItMatters: When one exhausted AI tries to build an entire app in one giant chat, it gets tired and forgets earlier details. Fresh, focused helpers working on separate pieces build faster, stay sharper, and never overwrite each other.
eli5.roleInProtocol: Station 4 is the engine room of the Code Factory. By separating the Planner from the Builders and keeping every helper inside its assigned files, your finished pieces snap together cleanly on the very first try.
eli5.howToUseGoingForward: Always complete shared setup files before launching parallel helpers, and make sure every builder runs a quick local checkup before handing work over to Station 5 Quality Inspection.
eli5.whenToUse: Use this right after your blueprint and floor plan are approved—whether you are using one focused helper for a small feature or a parallel team for a multi-part milestone.
eli5.realWorldExample: This very Academy upgrade used Station 4 live: the lead coordinator froze the shared course blueprint first, then four separate helpers upgraded all eight courses simultaneously—each editing only its own assigned course files with zero collisions.
eli5.audioScript: Now we reach Station Four: building side by side without stepping on anyone's toes. Picture four friends doing a giant jigsaw puzzle together. If everyone reaches for the exact same corner, elbows collide. Instead, you snap the shared border pieces into place first—we call that Step Zero—and then each friend calmly builds their own corner from the picture on the box. In our software factory, the lead helper finishes the shared connecting files first, then focused specialist helpers build their separate folders at the same time, following the locked blueprint closely. When they finish, everything snaps together cleanly for inspection.
eli5.diagramCaption: How locking shared connecting files first lets multiple specialist helpers build separate parts cleanly in parallel.

keyTakeaways: Separation of Concerns: The architect who writes the spec is decoupled from the builders implementing it, and builders never invent unapproved dependencies or routes.
Zero File Contention: Task 1 owns `scripts/`, `content/`, `src/lib/`, `src/data/`, and `src/app/api/`; Task 2 owns `src/components/three/`; Task 3 owns UI components; Task 4 owns `tests/`.
All business logic ships with strict TypeScript (zero `any`), runtime Zod validation, and deterministic pure functions (zero `child_process` in API routes).
actionChecklist: Inspect `skills/cf-implement/references/orchestration.md` to review the exact Swarm partitioning rules.
Run `pnpm run sync:resources` to verify the allowlisted build-time manifest regenerates cleanly with zero errors.
Verify local `pnpm typecheck && pnpm lint && pnpm test` before handing off to Stage 5 QA.

steps.title: Stage 5 — Test: Dual-Axis Evals (Output + Trajectory) & 3-Viewport QA
steps.summary: Verification is the line between vibe coding and engineering (Day 4 Security & Eval + Agentic Code Quality). Never let the generator grade its own homework: `cf-qa-review` + `cf-eval` audit BOTH final output AND execution trajectory via decoupled `cf-reviewer`, `cf-tester`, and `browser` agents.

eli5.plainTitle: Station 5: Independent Quality Check (Never Grade Your Own Homework)
eli5.oneLineHook: Bring in a fresh inspector who did not build the app to test both the finished screens and how honestly the work was done.
eli5.everydayAnalogy: A health inspector who both tastes the finished meal AND checks that the kitchen followed every clean-hands rule.
eli5.simpleExplanation: If you ask the same helper who built a page 'did you do a good job?' it will almost always say yes! Station 5 uses a strict rule: never let the builder grade its own homework. Three fresh inspectors step in—one runs every automated test, one reviews safety and house rules with fresh eyes, and one opens a real web browser at phone, tablet, and desktop sizes. They check BOTH the finished result AND that nobody took shortcuts or skipped checks.
eli5.whyItMatters: This single station is the line between messy trial-and-error and trustworthy software. Fresh eyes catch subtle phone-screen clipping, hard-to-read button colors, and hidden safety gaps before a single real user ever sees them.
eli5.roleInProtocol: Station 5 writes an official Pass/Fail Quality Report (`.memory/qa-report.md`). Station 6 Launch is strictly locked shut until every serious defect is fixed and re-checked.
eli5.howToUseGoingForward: Never trust a builder's cheerful 'All done!' message alone. Always run an independent check covering automated tests, safety review, and real phone, tablet, and desktop screens.
eli5.whenToUse: Use this right after building any feature and ALWAYS before sharing a preview link or publishing live to real users.
eli5.realWorldExample: During our real Academy build, fresh Station 5 inspectors caught four issues the builders missed: a button color that was slightly too faint to read easily, a first-frame 3D animation hiccup, a screen-reader label slip, and a stale cached image—all fixed cleanly before launch!
eli5.audioScript: Station Five is what separates quick guesswork from truly trustworthy software, and it follows one golden rule: never let a builder grade its own homework. Think of a restaurant inspector who does two separate checks—first tasting the finished dish, and second making sure the kitchen did not cut corners behind the scenes. Here, three fresh helpers step in who did not write the code. One runs every automatic test. One checks safety rules and confirms no tests were skipped. And one opens a real web browser at phone, tablet, and desktop sizes to verify every button looks crisp. Nothing reaches launch until this report is green.
eli5.diagramCaption: How three fresh inspectors check finished quality, honest process, and phone, tablet, and desktop screens before approving launch.

keyTakeaways: Verification Is the Narrow Neck: Generation is wide and cheap; moving quality into the harness (strict types, Zod boundaries, `cf-next-verify`, deterministic Vitest, SAST) prevents review overload.

Dual-Axis Evaluation (`cf-eval`): Grade BOTH Output Quality (tests, CVEs, contrast >= 4.5:1, valid ARIA) AND Execution Trajectory (spec adherence, zero oracle-gaming/disabled lints, zero desktop-vs-mobile blind spots).

Real Project_Antigravity Catches: Decoupled review caught Three.js negative-dt frame-1 crashes, cyan CTA contrast (< 4.5:1 -> fixed to 5.70:1), invalid `role="tablist"` nesting, and pnpm v11 ignored overrides.
Output is persisted to `.memory/qa-report.md`—Stage 6 Deploy is strictly blocked if any P0/P1 defect or trajectory violation remains.
actionChecklist: Inspect `agents/cf-reviewer.md` and `skills/cf-qa-review/SKILL.md` in the Repo Explorer.
Verify all 4 Vitest suites pass deterministically with zero flaky timers or network mocks leaking.
Confirm `.memory/qa-report.md` records explicit Pass clearance across security, tests, and all 3 responsive viewports.

steps.title: Stage 6 — Deploy: Rollback Plan, HITL Approval & Preview Smoke Tests
steps.summary: Day 5 ('Spec-Driven Production Grade Development') graduates local agents into governed, observable cloud deployments while humans Own the Outer Loop (Quality, Verdict, Answerability). `cf-deploy-staging` + `hooks/hitl-gate.py` enforce QA clearance, rollback plans, HITL approval, and live smoke tests.

eli5.plainTitle: Station 6: Safe Dress Rehearsal & Undo Button Before Going Live
eli5.oneLineHook: Write down your instant undo button first, pause for your human thumbs-up, and test a private preview link before opening the doors.
eli5.everydayAnalogy: Running a private theater dress rehearsal with the emergency curtain rope already in hand before opening night.
eli5.simpleExplanation: Putting your project onto the live internet is a big step, so Station 6 never rushes it. First, it checks that Station 5's Quality Report is completely green. Second, it writes down the exact one-line undo command before anything goes online. Third, a safety lock pauses and asks for your explicit human approval. Fourth, it launches a private practice preview link and runs quick live health checks to confirm every page responds fast.
eli5.whyItMatters: Publishing straight to real users without a preview link or an undo plan turns tiny cloud glitches into stressful emergencies. A calm dress rehearsal with a ready undo button keeps launches boring and safe.
eli5.roleInProtocol: Station 6 puts you firmly in charge of the final Launch Verdict. Automatic safety locks (`hooks/hitl-gate.py`) block unapproved live publishes so an AI can never push unfinished work to your real users behind your back.
eli5.howToUseGoingForward: Make three rules unbreakable for every launch: green Quality Report first, written undo command second, and test a private preview link before ever flipping the public switch.
eli5.whenToUse: Use this anytime you are ready to share a working version online—first to a private staging preview link, and later when promoting to your public live address.
eli5.realWorldExample: Before publishing a new Academy course update, your helper checks that all tests passed, writes the exact one-line rollback command into your handover note, pauses for your 'Yes, deploy preview,' and verifies the live preview link answers within five seconds.
eli5.audioScript: Station Six is launch day—done the calm, stress-free way. Think of opening night at a theater: you never raise the curtain for a packed crowd without a private dress rehearsal and a clear plan if a stage light flickers. First, Station Six confirms your Quality Report from Station Five is completely green. Second, it writes down your exact one-step undo button before anything leaves your computer. Third, a built-in safety lock pauses and waits for your explicit human approval. Finally, it publishes a private preview link and runs a fast live checkup so you know everything works on the real internet before inviting users in.
eli5.diagramCaption: How Station 6 verifies green checks, prepares your undo button, pauses for your approval, and tests a private preview link.

keyTakeaways: Own the Outer Loop (Quality / Verdict / Answerability): Before approving any staging or production deploy, verify harness quality evidence, issue an explicit human Verdict, and be answerable for why the change is safe.

Human-in-the-Loop Gate: `hooks/hitl-gate.py` enforces `force_ask` on `vercel --prod`, `wrangler deploy`, `supabase db push`, and `git push`, while `hooks/secret-guard.py` blocks accidental credential writes.
Rollback-First Discipline: Document the exact `vercel rollback <deployment-url>` command in `.memory/handover.md` *before* triggering a deployment.
Post-Deploy Smoke Test: Validate live HTTP 200 on `/`, `/api/courses`, `/api/resources`, and `POST /api/hitl/simulate` on the deployed staging preview URL.
actionChecklist: Verify `.memory/qa-report.md` contains zero blocking defects before requesting staging deploy approval.
Test `vercel deploy` (staging preview) vs. `vercel --prod` (force_ask) in the live HITL Gate Simulator.
Record the staging preview URL, rollback command, and smoke-test results in `.memory/handover.md`.

codeSnippet.code:
# 1. Deploy staging preview (after human approval)
cd academy && vercel deploy

# 2. Smoke-test live API contracts (<= 5000ms timeout invariant)
curl --max-time 5 -sf "$STAGING_URL/api/courses?limit=5" | jq '.total'
curl --max-time 5 -sf "$STAGING_URL/api/resources?category=skill&limit=20" | jq '.total'
curl --max-time 5 -sf -X POST "$STAGING_URL/api/hitl/simulate" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"commandLine":"git push --force"}' | jq '.decision'

steps.title: Stage 7 — User Feedback: Structured Triage & Severity Backlog
steps.summary: Real learners and staging telemetry always surface edge cases that unit tests miss. Stage 7 (`cf-triage`) classifies feedback and runtime logs by severity (P0–P3), isolates root causes, and queues actionable items in `.memory/tasks.md`.

eli5.plainTitle: Station 7: Listen to Real Users & Sort What to Fix First
eli5.oneLineHook: Real people always spot surprises automated checks missed—sort every note calmly from urgent fixes down to future wish-list ideas.
eli5.everydayAnalogy: A hospital front desk sorting urgent emergencies ahead of routine checkups so critical issues never wait.
eli5.simpleExplanation: Once real people click around your preview or live app, they will always notice helpful things you never expected—a confusing button label, a glitch on a small phone, or a fun feature idea. Station 7 keeps you from panicking or patching randomly. It sorts every report calmly by urgency (from urgent broken features down to nice-to-have wishes), traces the real root cause, and adds clear next steps to your project's task list.
eli5.whyItMatters: Trying to fix ten random comments at once creates new bugs and burnout. Calm sorting ensures urgent broken items get repaired right away while creative feature wishes queue neatly for the next planned cycle.

eli5.plainTitle: Bonus Guardrail: Living Feature Maps & Code Floor-Plan Fences
eli5.oneLineHook: Keep one live map of every screen so a robot checks them all automatically—and put up walls so buttons can never grab secret server pipes.
eli5.everydayAnalogy: A restaurant's master menu checklist paired with solid walls separating the dining room from the kitchen gas lines.
eli5.simpleExplanation: As an app grows, two sneaky problems appear: an edit on one page quietly breaks another page, or a visual button accidentally reaches into private server wiring. Code Factory stops both automatically. A Living Feature Map lists every screen and address in one tidy file so an automated checker tests phone, tablet, and desktop views in seconds. And Code Fences act like solid walls warning you right away if folders ever cross forbidden lines.
eli5.whyItMatters: Without a living map and automatic folder walls, teams only discover broken pages or tangled spaghetti code weeks later—usually right when a real customer clicks a broken button.
eli5.roleInProtocol: This upgrades Stage 4/5 Verification (`cf-verify-map` + `depcruise` inside `verify-stack.sh`). Whenever routes or buttons change, you update `.memory/feature-map.md` in the same commit, and automated checks verify zero console errors, zero overflow, and zero boundary leaks.
eli5.howToUseGoingForward: Keep one short Feature Map file in `.memory/` listing every key screen and address—never storing passwords there—and run your Feature Map check plus Architecture Fence check before every pull request or live deploy.
eli5.whenToUse: Use this right after editing any webpage layout, route, or API endpoint, or whenever your app grows past a handful of files and you want automatic protection against spaghetti imports and broken screens.
eli5.realWorldExample: You rename a button section on your Course page. eli5.audioScript: As your app grows beyond a couple of pages, two sneaky problems love to creep in. First, fixing one screen quietly breaks another screen you forgot to click. Second, quick edits tangle your folders together so visual buttons accidentally reach straight into private database pipes. Code Factory version two point four solves both with two simple habits. First, keep a Living Feature Map—like a restaurant's master menu checklist listing every screen and key element—so an automated tester opens every page across phone, tablet, and desktop in seconds and saves a screenshot if anything breaks. Second, put up automatic Architecture Fences that catch tangled circular loops or secret server leaks before your code ever leaves your laptop.
eli5.diagramCaption: How a Living Feature Map and Architecture Fences catch broken screens, missing elements, and forbidden folder crossings automatically.

keyTakeaways: Living Feature Map (`.memory/feature-map.md`): Combines human-readable Golden Happy Paths with an embedded fenced `json feature-map` contract (routes, HTTP status codes, key selectors, 375/768/1440px overflow checks) with zero plaintext credentials.

steps.title: v3.0.0 Core Hooks — 5-Event Lifecycle Guardrails, Auto-Hydration & Stop Gate
steps.summary: Code Factory v3.0.0 activates five native Antigravity lifecycle events using pure Python 3 stdlib and an atomic 0600 per-conversation state store (`hooks/hook_state.py`): `SessionStart` `.memory/` hydration, fail-closed `PreToolUse` HITL (+ safe `overwrite`) & secret guard, `PostToolUse` -> `PreInvocation` `<2s` single-file lint, turn-15+ compaction nudges & 5-failure loop-breaker, and a bounded single-shot `Stop` verification gate.

eli5.plainTitle: Automatic Safety Net: 5 Built-In Checkpoints Across Every AI Session
eli5.oneLineHook: Five quiet background checkpoints greet your session with fresh notes, guard risky commands, spot typos in 2 seconds, stop error loops, and check tests before finishing.
eli5.everydayAnalogy: A smart airplane cockpit with pre-flight notes, safety switches, instant alerts, autopilot brakes, and a landing checklist.
eli5.simpleExplanation: Think of every AI coding session like a short flight with five helpful cockpit checkpoints. When the session opens, Checkpoint 1 hands your AI today's handover notes and folder status. Before any command or file save runs, Checkpoint 2 blocks passwords and pauses on risky moves while adding safe defaults. Right after an edit, Checkpoints 3 and 4 run a 2-second spellcheck and halt endless error loops. Finally, Checkpoint 5 reminds your AI once to run tests before landing.
eli5.whyItMatters: Without automatic lifecycle checkpoints, you have to babysit every session by hand—pasting handover notes, chasing silent syntax typos, stopping runaway retry loops, and remembering to ask whether tests actually ran.
eli5.roleInProtocol: This is the v3.0.0 Phase 1 Core Hooks engine registered in hooks.json and backed by hooks/hook_state.py. Every hook uses pure Python standard library with zero external packages, strict per-conversation 0600 isolation, and instant environment-variable kill switches.
eli5.howToUseGoingForward: Let all five hooks run quietly in the background on every project. Keep .memory/handover.md concise so SessionStart loads fast, watch for PreInvocation turn-15 compaction tips, and use CF_* environment switches if you ever need to pause one hook.
eli5.whenToUse: Active automatically on every Antigravity session once the Code Factory v3.0.0 plugin is linked—ideal for daily feature builds, parallel swarms, and safe production maintenance.
eli5.realWorldExample: You open a fresh chat and SessionStart loads your 2 KB handover note automatically. You edit a TypeScript file with a missing brace; two seconds later PostToolUse hands a clean note to PreInvocation, the AI fixes it, and Stop reminds it once to run tests before finishing.
eli5.audioScript: Welcome to Code Factory version three, where five automatic checkpoints quietly protect every single session from takeoff to landing. Picture a modern airplane cockpit. First, at session start, the preflight briefing hands your helper your short handover note and current folder status automatically. Second, before any tool runs, safety switches block leaked passwords, pause for your approval on dangerous commands, and gently add safe defaults like non-blocking git output and five-second web timeouts. Third and fourth, right after saving a file, a fast two-second checker scans that single file and passes a crisp note to the next turn, while also halting runaway loops after five identical failures and nudging you to tidy long chats at turn fifteen. Finally, before the session ends, a single-shot landing checklist reminds your helper once to verify edited code with real tests.
eli5.diagramCaption: How all five v3.0.0 lifecycle hooks coordinate through the private atomic state store from session start to verified finish.

keyTakeaways: 5 Native Events in `hooks.json`: Flat arrays for `SessionStart`, `PreInvocation`, and `Stop`; grouped `{matcher, hooks}` arrays for `PreToolUse` (`hitl-gate.py`, `secret-guard.py`) and `PostToolUse` (`post-tool-feedback.py`).

Atomic Private State (`hooks/hook_state.py`): Pure Python 3 stdlib stores per-conversation JSON under `$PLUGIN_DATA/conversations/<cid>.json` with `0700`/`0600` perms, strict `conversationId` sanitization, secret redaction, and `24h` TTL pruning.

Fail-Closed vs. Fail-Open Separation: `PreToolUse` security gates fail closed (`ask`/`deny`, never `{}`) and apply conservative `overwrite` (`git --no-pager`, `curl --max-time 5`) only on safe allowed commands; DX hooks (`SessionStart`, `PostToolUse`, `PreInvocation`, `Stop`) never brick the agent loop.

Bounded Guarantees & Kill Switches: `PreInvocation` breaks 5-failure runaway loops (`terminationBehavior: "terminate"`) and nudges compaction at turn 15/30; `Stop` enforces a single-shot verification prompt guarding `NO_TOOL_CALL`, `continuationActive == false`, and `fullyIdle == true`; every hook can be toggled via `hooks.json` or `CF_*` env vars.
actionChecklist: Inspect `hooks.json` and `hooks/hook_state.py` in the Live Repo Explorer to trace all 5 lifecycle hooks and atomic `0600` state isolation.
Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s hooks -p "test_*.py" -v` to verify every security, overwrite, lint-bridge, loop-breaker, and stop-gate invariant locally.
Keep `.memory/handover.md` under 3 KB so `SessionStart` hydrates clean workspace context in under 1.5 seconds.

codeSnippet.filename: Verify v3.0.0 Core Hooks & Zero-Code Runtime Kill Switches
codeSnippet.code:
# 1. Run the full pure-stdlib Python hook verification suite
python3 -m unittest discover -s hooks -p "test_*.py" -v

# 2. Optional zero-code runtime kill switches (no file edits needed)
export CF_HITL_OVERWRITE=off       # Disable automatic git --no-pager / curl --max-time 5
export CF_POST_TOOL_LINT=off       # Skip <2s single-file lint in PostToolUse
export CF_LOOP_BREAKER_MAX=0       # Disable 5-failure runaway loop-breaker
export CF_CONTEXT_WARN_TURN=0      # Disable turn-15/30 compaction reminders
export CF_STOP_GATE_MODE=off       # Disable single-shot Stop verification prompt

Execute `skills/cf-verify-map/SKILL.md` for `{{app_dir}}` served at `{{base_url}}`:

1. Create or update `.memory/feature-map.md` listing our key routes (`{{routes_to_check}}`), API health/contracts, key DOM selectors, and Golden Happy Paths—strictly zero plaintext passwords or secrets.
2. Run the deterministic Feature Map verifier (`run-verify-map.mjs --map .memory/feature-map.md --all-viewports`) across `375px`, `768px`, and `1440px` (falling back cleanly to the `browser` subagent if Playwright is not installed).
3. Output the structured Feature Map Verification Report showing console errors, page errors, `4xx/5xx` network failures, missing selectors, horizontal overflow, and any failure screenshot paths.
prompts.expectedOutcome: An up-to-date `.memory/feature-map.md` contract and a deterministic PASS/FAIL multi-viewport verification report with zero regressions.

prompts.title: Add Automated Architecture Boundary Fences (dependency-cruiser)
prompts.eli5Title: Add Automatic Code Fences to Stop Spaghetti Loops & UI-to-Server Leaks
prompts.description: Configures `.dependency-cruiser.cjs` and `arch:check` so `verify-stack.sh` (Step 4b) automatically blocks circular imports, UI-to-database/server leaks, and domain-to-UI coupling.
prompts.whenToUse: Copy this as soon as a project grows past a few folders so automated checks immediately block circular bugs or visual components importing server-only secrets.
prompts.template:
Set up automated Architecture Boundary Fences for `{{app_dir}}` using `skills/cf-verify-map/resources/dependency-cruiser.template.cjs`:

1. Inspect `{{src_dir}}` module layers (UI components, domain/lib, API routes, feature slices) and tailor `.dependency-cruiser.cjs` enforcing: `no-circular`, `no-server-or-db-in-ui`, `no-lib-importing-app-or-ui`, and `no-cross-feature-imports`.
2. Ask for my approval before installing `dependency-cruiser` as a devDependency if missing, then add `"arch:check": "depcruise src --config .dependency-cruiser.cjs"` to `package.json`.
3. Run `pnpm run arch:check` and `skills/cf-next-verify/scripts/verify-stack.sh` to confirm Step 4b passes with zero boundary violations.
prompts.expectedOutcome: An automated `arch:check` boundary gate wired into `verify-stack.sh` guaranteeing zero circular imports or UI-to-server leaks.

prompts.title: Verify & Tune Code Factory v3.0.0 5-Event Core Hooks
prompts.eli5Title: Test & Configure All 5 Automatic Safety & Quality Checkpoints
prompts.description: Audits the 5-event v3.0.0 Core Hooks registry (SessionStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreInvocation, Stop), runs deterministic stdlib Python unit tests, and verifies CF_* runtime kill switches.
prompts.whenToUse: Copy this after linking or upgrading the Code Factory v3.0.0 plugin, or whenever you want to verify hook latency, secret redaction, safe overwrite rules, and kill switches.
prompts.template:
Audit and verify the Enterprise Code Factory v3.0.0 5-event Core Hooks under `{{hooks_dir}}`:

1. Validate `hooks.json` against `agy-customizations/docs/hooks.md` (named top-level hooks, flat arrays for `SessionStart`/`PreInvocation`/`Stop`, grouped `{matcher, hooks}` arrays for `PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse`, and `timeout: 5`).
2. Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s {{hooks_dir}} -p "test_*.py" -v` and confirm 100% pass across `hitl-gate.py` (`force_ask` + safe `overwrite`), `secret-guard.py`, `hook_state.py` (`0600` atomic store + redaction), `session-start.py`, `post-tool-feedback.py`, `pre-invocation.py` (loop-breaker threshold `{{loop_breaker_max}}`), and `stop-gate.py`.
3. Verify our desired runtime toggle profile (`{{kill_switch_mode}}`) and confirm `rules/AGENTS.md` remains strictly `<= 10240` bytes (`wc -c rules/AGENTS.md`).
prompts.expectedOutcome: A passing Python stdlib hook test report confirming all 5 lifecycle events, atomic 0600 state isolation, latency budgets, and kill-switch behavior.

prompts.title: Distill a Resolved Bug Into a Permanent Rule & Regression Test (cf-learn)
prompts.eli5Title: Turn a Fixed Bug Into a Permanent House Rule So It Never Returns
prompts.description: Extracts the systemic root-cause pattern from a resolved bug or post-mortem into a permanent invariant rule and deterministic regression test requirement.
prompts.whenToUse: Copy this right after fixing any tricky bug, UI glitch, or security issue so you lock in one house rule and test preventing that failure forever.
prompts.template:
Execute Stage 6B (`cf-learn`) for the resolved incident below:

- Resolved bug or incident: {{incident_summary}}
- Systemic root-cause invariant to enforce: {{root_cause_rule}}
- Target rule file: `{{rule_target_file}}`
- Regression test file: `{{regression_test_file}}`

Steps:
1. Inspect the fix diff and verify we capture the systemic root-cause pattern rather than a one-off symptom.
2. Draft a concise, enforceable permanent rule entry for `{{rule_target_file}}` (keeping global `rules/AGENTS.md <= 10 KB` if targeting global rules).
3. Confirm or add a deterministic regression test in `{{regression_test_file}}` covering the exact failure mode.
4. Present the proposed rule and test check for my explicit human approval before editing rule files, then verify the Stage 6B Sign-Off Gate.

variables.label: Resolved Bug / Incident
variables.placeholder: Describe the bug, UI glitch, or security issue you resolved
variables.defaultValue: ESLint v9 rejected --format compact inside post-tool-feedback.py

variables.label: Root-Cause Invariant Rule
variables.placeholder: What permanent guardrail prevents this failure class?
variables.defaultValue: Use ESLint v9-compatible --format stylish and cover hook formatter output with unit tests

prompts.expectedOutcome: A concise permanent invariant rule ready for explicit approval plus a deterministic regression test proving the resolved failure mode cannot silently recur.
